name: Sulpiride
summary: Sulpiride (Dolmatil, Dogmatil) is an antipsychotic used at higher doses for schizophrenia and at lower doses for depression and some stomach and dizziness problems; it is not approved in the United States.
description: Sulpiride, sold under brand names including Dolmatil and Dogmatil, is an antipsychotic (a substituted benzamide) that selectively blocks dopamine D2 and D3 receptors. At higher doses, it is used to treat schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders, while at lower doses it may be prescribed for depression, long-lasting low mood (dysthymia), and ongoing indigestion with no clear cause (dyspepsia). It is also sometimes used to treat vertigo (a spinning dizziness). Sulpiride is not approved in the United States but is widely used in Europe, Asia, and South America.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Sulpiride, sold under brand names including Dolmatil and Dogmatil, is a substituted benzamide antipsychotic that selectively antagonizes dopamine D2 and D3 receptors. At higher doses, it is used in the management of schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders, while at lower doses it may be prescribed for depression, dysthymia, and functional dyspepsia. It is also sometimes used to treat vertigo. Sulpiride is not approved in the United States but is widely used in Europe, Asia, and South America.
